Spotlight: Help Northside Toyota fill the Tundra for local food programs
sum: An extra item in your grocery cart can become part of a truckload of support for neighbours in Sault Ste. Marie.

Northside Toyota’s Fill the Tundra campaign is collecting donations until Dec. 11 for the Soup Kitchen Community Centre and St. Vincent Place. Now in its 12th year, the campaign is inviting the community to help reach its $20,000 goal through combined monetary donations and non-perishable food items that will fill the trucks.
Watch Mario Palumbo, dealer principal at Northside Toyota, share how Fill the Tundra began and how you can support this year’s campaign.
The campaign started when Northside Toyota moved into its Great Northern Road facility. Staff wanted to support local food programs, and the dealership’s largest vehicle gave them an idea.

“We wanted to give back to the community that supports us, and the biggest vehicle we had was a Tundra,” says Mario Palumbo, dealer principal at Northside Toyota. “We thought, ‘Let’s fill it.’ What started with one truck grew as more people got involved.”
Over its history, Fill the Tundra has collected more than $100,000 in monetary and non-perishable donations, with the community typically filling two or three trucks each year.
Customers dropping off food, staff making deliveries and the welcome from the recipient organizations have all become memorable parts of the campaign.

items.t: JTEKT tender targets 11mn shares as Toyota says it will offer 10mn
sum: JTEKT's board resolved on November 25, 2026 to buy back shares through a tender offer at ¥1,733 each, and Toyota has told the company it intends to tender 10 million shares, or 3.14% of the total. The two sides have not signed a tender agreement.

Terms. The price is a 10% discount to the November 24 close of ¥1,925. The offer runs from November 26 to December 23 (20 business days), with settlement starting January 21, 2027. JTEKT plans to buy 11 million shares (3.45%) and has capped the board authorization at 11,000,100. It wants total spending within ¥20bn and expects to need about ¥19.1bn. The funds come from its own cash.

Toyota's stake. Toyota holds 77,235,087 shares, or 24.26%. Talks began with a plan for Toyota to tender 9 million shares. JTEKT said the share price since its first approach on October 26 would have left spending short of ¥20bn on that number, so it asked on November 13 about 10 million, and Toyota agreed on November 25.

If total acceptances exceed 11 million shares, purchases will be pro rata, so part of Toyota's tendered stake would go unbought. Toyota told JTEKT it has not decided when or how it would sell any such shares, and that it intends to keep holding the shares it does not tender.

Conflict controls. A JTEKT director who also holds a senior Toyota post stayed out of the board's deliberation and vote and out of the talks with Toyota. The president, who spent 30 years or more at Toyota before moving to JTEKT, did the same.

Cancellation. JTEKT plans to cancel 9.5 million of the repurchased shares on February 15, 2027, but only if it acquires more than 9.5 million in the tender. That would leave 309,108,107 shares in issue. For shares beyond 9.5 million, JTEKT says it will consider using them to reward employees.

items.t: Toyota Land Cruiser FJ gets tasty off-road upgrades from Kuhl Racing
sum: Japanese tuner Kuhl Racing has handed the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ a selection of off-road equipment and modifications.

In January 2026, Kuhl Racing unveiled a beefed-up Toyota Land Cruiser Prado featuring a raft of off-road gear and modifications. Now, the Japanese tuner has applied its know-how to the most compact member in the Land Cruiser family, the Land Cruiser FJ.

The new range of equipment available for the J240 generation includes off-road bumpers, front and rear, an ACC Easy-Up suspension spacer kit, and 18-inch Verz-Kross VK01 alloy wheels wrapped in Dunlop Grandtrek RT01 tyres. Customers also have the choice of rectangular or retro-inspired round headlamps.

In the future, Kuhl Racing will expand the equipment list to include a steel bull bar featuring an LED light bar, more suspension upgrades, upgraded braking systems, and a supercharger kit. Sportier items will also be introduced, such as roof-mounted rear spoiler and quad exhaust outlets.

As a reminder, the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ shares its IMV (Innovative International Multi-purpose Vehicle) ladder-frame platform with the Hilux and Fortuner. The J240 is exclusively equipped with the 2TR-FE 2.7-litre naturally aspirated four-cylinder petrol engine, tuned to produce 122 kW and 245 N.m of torque.
The powertrain is paired with a part-time 4×4 system, coupled with a six-speed automatic transmission featuring a low-range transfer case. A rear diff-lock is also present.
The J240 sports a 245 mm ground clearance. The approach and departure angles are rated at 29 and 38 degrees, respectively.

items.t: Honda and Toyota Recall 1.6 Million Vehicles Over Takata Airbags
sum: Honda and Toyota are recalling approximately 1.6 million vehicles equipped with Takata airbags because defective inflators could rupture and send metal fragments into passenger compartments. The recalls cover older Honda and Toyota models in the United States and international markets, according to information from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

The recall affects 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the United States, along with approximately 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide. Of the Toyota vehicles included, 314,000 are located in the United States.

According to the NHTSA report, a ruptured inflator could cause metal fragments to penetrate the airbag cushion, potentially resulting in serious injuries or fatalities. The agency noted that none of the vehicles covered by this recall had been the subject of a warranty claim, and no injuries or deaths had been reported.
The Toyota recall includes the 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 Lexus IS250, 2017 Lexus GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Toyota Tundra, 2005-2007 Toyota Sequoia, and 2016-2017 Toyota 4Runner.
Honda's affected models include certain 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX, and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles.
The NHTSA report describes the potential consequences of an inflator failure:
"In the event of an inflator rupture, metal fragments could pass through the airbag cushion material possibly causing serious injury or fatality to vehicle occupants." the agency stated.

sum: The issue has to do with Takata front passenger airbag inflators that are nearing the end of their estimated safe service life. The NHTSA said the inflators could rupture owing to propellant degradation after long-term exposure to high humidity and high temperatures.
In case the front passenger airbag deploys in a car crash, the worn out inflator could burst and send sharp metal fragments into the car cabin at high speed.
The NHTSA has said that authorized Toyota and Lexus dealers will replace the front passenger airbag inflator or the entire airbag assembly free of cost, depending on your vehicle.

Toyota is planning to mail owner notification letters between December 28, 2026 and January 11, 2027, according to the NHTSA report cited by Fox Business. However, owners do not have to wait for the letters to contact a dealer regarding replacements.

2027 Toyota Sequoia and Tundra: A Welcome Update
sum: Frisco, Texas–Toyota simply cannot match the American dominance of the full-size vehicle segment, but that doesn't mean customers should avoid the Sequoia and Tundra. In fact, if the Japanese giant wants to capture the attention of Canadians, it needs to keep investing in and refining its body-on-frame lineup, which also includes the 4Runner, Tacoma and Land Cruiser. At this Texas presentation not far from Toyota's North American headquarters in Dallas, the spotlight was firmly on its two biggest offerings.

For 2027, Toyota introduces the first mid-cycle updates to both the Sequoia and Tundra. Unsurprisingly, the fundamentals remain unchanged, but both vehicles gain a more distinctive personality, improved off-road capabilities and more sophisticated towing technology.
- Toyota’s SEMA-Bound Snowhunters Would Crush Canadian Winters
- Toyota Delays Highlander EV, Gives Sequoia New Tech and Trailhunter Model

While the Tundra and Sequoia share much of their mechanical DNA, their respective missions are quite different. The former is primarily a workhorse that also enjoys playing the adventurer, while the latter aims to combine the attributes of a large family SUV with those of an expedition vehicle.

Toyota has revised the exterior of both models for 2027. The changes hardly amount to a design revolution, but their new front ends make it impossible to deny the family resemblance, thanks to a grille that is nearly identical. Beyond that, however, the company has left just about everything else untouched, aside perhaps from the available exterior colours and wheel designs. We got a closer look at a new paint colour called Honeycomb, which can be ordered on all vehicles built on the TNGA-F platform, including the Land Cruiser, 4Runner, Tacoma, Sequoia and Tundra.

Inside, the changes are subtler, although the redesigned steering wheel brings a welcome touch of freshness to the driving environment. Toyota has retained a familiar dashboard layout, which isn't necessarily a bad thing in vehicles designed to work as hard as they haul families. All trim levels now feature the larger 14-inch touchscreen, while the 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster is also standard starting with the Sequoia SR5 TRD Off-Road and the Tundra SR.

items.t: Nvidia Stock Drops 9.5% as CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal
sum: A sharp decline of approximately 9.5% hit Nvidia’s stock over two trading sessions on November 9th and 10th, erasing nearly $430 billion in market capitalization. This financial drop followed the emergence of images showing CEO Jensen Huang with a woman, an event that triggered the most significant crisis of his career.

Nvidia’s board of directors announced an independent investigation earlier this week after reports suggested Huang might have been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company stated there is currently no basis to believe its technological secrets or U.S. national security were compromised.

Huang initially insisted he would continue leading the firm when the first scandal broke. However, after a second issue was exposed on November 12th, the board held an emergency meeting to consider removing him from the directorship. On that same day, Huang resigned as CEO.

During trading on November 12th in the US, Nvidia shares briefly lost over 14% of their value before closing down 4.3%. The sell-off extended to many AI-related stocks, while rivals AMD and Broadcom saw their share prices rise, indicating a market reassessment of the competitive landscape.

Tim Oechsner, a capital markets expert at Steubing AG, noted that Huang is not only the CEO but also the face of the AI revolution. His resignation has caused market disruption, weakening investor sentiment and shifting focus to future developments.

Concerns extend beyond stock prices due to Nvidia’s central role in the AI ecosystem. According to Reuters, some suppliers have begun reconsidering expansion plans, fearing a successor may not maintain Huang’s aggressive growth strategy. AP correspondent Kelvin Chan highlighted that Nvidia plays a key role in the artificial intelligence competition between the US and China, with its graphics processors subject to strict export restrictions.

The situation echoes past corporate collapses where leadership instability threatened entire enterprises. In 2019, startup WeWork was valued at $47 billion under founder Adam Neumann. Excessive power, conflict-of-interest deals, and mounting losses led to the cancellation of its IPO plans and Neumann’s departure.

items.t: Fortuner vs Kodiaq vs Tayron: How Toyota's ladder-frame icon stacks up against majestor
sum: Fortuner vs Kodiaq vs Tayron: Toyota’s next Fortuner is expected to debut globally on December 1, with an India launch in 2027, but the current model already faces its toughest competition in years.

Toyota’s next Fortuner is expected to make its global debut on December 1, but the SUV it replaces is already facing its toughest fight in years. One report says the Fortuner has held an almost unchallenged position in India’s full-size diesel 4x4 segment for nearly two decades. That grip is now loosening from several directions at once. MG has replaced the Gloster with the Majestor, which it prices to rival the Fortuner. Skoda has updated the Kodiaq with an ADAS suite and a lower starting price. Volkswagen has added the Tayron R-Line as its flagship. Each rival attacks in a different way: on price, on luxury or on off-road hardware. With the new Fortuner expected in India in 2027, buyers have a rare chance to weigh all four side by side. Here is how they compare

The baseline: Toyota FortunerThe Fortuner runs a 2.8-litre diesel. It makes 201bhp and 500Nm. The standard 4x4 diesel automatic costs Rs 43.12 lakh, while the Legender is Rs 48.29 lakh and the GR-S Rs 50.46 lakh. The cheapest 4x2 diesel automatic is Rs 37.61 lakh.

This is the rival that most directly targets Toyota's formula. It replaces the Gloster and is priced from Rs 40.99 lakh. Its 2.0-litre twin-turbo diesel makes 215hp and 479Nm, sent to all four wheels through an 8-speed automatic. The top 4x4 costs Rs 44.99 lakh, undercutting the Fortuner Legender and GR-S. The standard Fortuner 4x4 is still Rs 1.87 lakh cheaper than the fully loaded Majestor. It also brings Level 2 ADAS and a long equipment list.

The Kodiaq goes a different way. It starts at Rs 36.99 lakh, and ADAS is available on the Sportline and Selection L&K trims. It uses a 2.0-litre turbo-petrol making 201 bhp and 320 Nm. There is no diesel option in India. That suits city and highway use, but it gives up the Fortuner's torque and tow-and-trail image. Power goes to all four wheels through a seven-speed DSG.

The Tayron aims higher up the ladder. It launched at an introductory Rs 46.99 lakh with 14 Level 2 ADAS functions and nine airbags. It is essentially a three-row version of the Tiguan R-Line, built at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

sum: Jim Farley keeps pitching bold growth targets for Ford while Wall Street responds by punishing the stock harder than almost any major automaker. Something in his vision and the reality of the market is not adding up.

Ford (NASDAQ: F | F Price Prediction) CEO Jim Farley has been extremely optimistic about the No. 2 US car company’s prospects. That ignored stiffening competition as legacy car companies, beaten back by poor sales, have slowly reentered the US market, which he also abandoned. Add Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) to the mix. US EV sales are down 30% in the first nine months of this year. Car sales in the US are generally flat. The average age of a car on the road in the US is 12 years. The average new car price is $51,000.

Farley told many of his workers that his goal was to raise Ford’s unit sales by 20% by 2032. The WSJ reported, “The company’s global strategy turns on Farley’s emphasis on no longer making “boring” vehicles, which for now has left it without the budget-friendly small sedans and SUVs it used to give priority to.” However, other car companies are likely to abandon their “boring” models as well.
Wall St. has had enough of Ford’s sales and forecast, driving the stock down 38% in the last five years. The S&P is up 61% over the same period.

And Ford’s sales in the US are falling. It has far from modest sales in China and the EU. It is stuck in America.

sum: The Toyota 2JZ has earned a reputation as one of the import performance world’s most durable foundations, but Jay Meagher of RS Garage sees its appeal as something more than simply an engine capable of surviving four-digit horsepower.

To Meagher, the 2JZ is almost the Japanese equivalent of the small block Chevy – a well-engineered, versatile platform that responds to relatively straightforward modifications and can deliver impressive power without requiring the builder to reinvent the entire engine.

“You can take a stock one, tune it properly if it’s a turbo 2JZ engine, and you can make seven or 800 horsepower for a large block of time,” Meagher says. “From there, if you want to go up a level, you can put pistons and rods in one, some valve springs, some camshafts, and you’ve got a really good 1,000-horsepower engine.”

For this particular Engine of the Week build, however, Meagher took the combination a step further. The RS Garage 2JZ uses a 94mm-stroke Brian Crower crankshaft, Brian Crower titanium connecting rods and custom-spec CP pistons. Combined with the engine’s variable intake cam, the stroker rotating assembly is intended to produce the kind of broad powerband Meagher considers ideal for a 1,000-1,200-horsepower street car.
That distinction matters. Jay has experience with 2JZ combinations producing considerably more horsepower, but he doesn’t necessarily consider a bigger number to be a better street engine.
“I think the best use for the engine is in that 1,000-1,200 horsepower range because you can build a nice engine that lives,” he says.

The engine’s 94mm stroke is a significant departure from the factory 86mm dimension, and Meagher recommends the stroker approach for many street-oriented customers because of what the additional displacement does for turbo response and drivability.

sum: Ask anyone building an electric air taxi what actually keeps their program grounded, and the honest answer rarely involves rotors, batteries, or flight software. It's the assembly line.
Building One Aircraft Is Easy. Building Ten Thousand Is the Real Test

Aerospace companies have plenty of experience building a handful of incredible aircraft by hand. What almost none of them have done is build thousands of identical units consistently, safely, and cheaply enough that a ride actually pencils out financially.

That gap is the real story behind the joint venture Joby Aviation just formed with Toyota Motor Corporation, even though the official language is dressed up in talk of bringing air mobility to everyone. Building one exceptional aircraft proves an engineering team is brilliant. Building the ten-thousandth identical one proves a factory is.

Toyota has quietly backed Joby for close to a decade, contributing hundreds of millions of dollars across multiple funding rounds while loaning engineers to help with everything from seat design to production tooling. What changed this week isn't the size of the relationship — it's the shape of it.

Instead of acting as a financial backer watching from the sidelines, Toyota is now co-owner of a joint venture created specifically to industrialize Joby's aircraft. That's a fundamentally different bet. items.t: $38B Toyota Deal Proposed After Massive Pressure From Activist Investors
sum: Big privatization deals tend to go pretty smoothly in Japan. The minority shareholders grumble a bit initially, maybe even push back a little, but ultimately they have to accept whatever's put on the table by the larger companies. But Toyota has just learnt the hard way that this dynamic could be changing.

The Japanese automaking giant has essentially been strong-armed by Elliott Investment Management, one of the largest activist funds in the world, into paying 20,600 yen per share in its attempt to take Toyota Industries private. Toyota Industries is the company behind Toyota-branded products like jet looms and forklifts, and is actually the world's largest manufacturer of the latter. This deal would take Toyota Industries' valuation up to roughly $37.8 billion.

But how did this happen? To understand that, we'll have to go back to June 2025. That's when the Toyota group first proposed buying out Toyota Industries at 16,300 yen a share. Minority shareholders were not happy about the deal, and some overseas investors even went so far as to take the matter directly to the Tokyo Stock Exchange, as Reuters reported. That's when Elliott stepped in and started buying shares. As of the filing on March 2, it had built up a 7.7% stake worth around $3 billion.

Elliott didn't just buy shares; it also ran an aggressive campaign, releasing its own plan for Toyota Industries that painted a future where the company's shares could hit more than 40,000 yen a share. Toyota tried to hold the line: In January, it raised the offer to 18,800 yen, later claiming that it was the "best possible price." But that wasn't enough, and it later had to increase the offer by another 9.6%, a price to which Elliott finally agreed.

So Elliott got its price and agreed to tender its shares. But for the rest of the minority shareholders still holding stock in Toyota Industries, the picture isn't quite as rosy. Toyota and Toyota Industries had pitched the buyout as a way for the latter to shift its focus towards advanced mobility technology without being weighed down by short-term profit expectations. That's the upside, at least in theory. What it doesn't address, though, are the concerns that several analysts and investors have raised about the deal, as reported by outlets such as Reuters.

sum: - In today’s CEO Daily: Diane Brady speaks with a CEO about his devotion to lean manufacturing.
- The big leadership story: Job-hopping isn’t paying off like it used to.
- The markets: Mixed globally as U.K. and European markets end their recent rallies.

Good morning. Nothing screams ‘yesterday’s man’ (or woman) like talking about kaizens and lean manufacturing. The continuous-improvement program made famous by Toyota in the 1950s was embraced by corporate America before many of us got our first job. Today GE Aerospace CEO Larry Culp is an ardent proponent, as are Ford’s Jim Farley and Baxter International chief Andrew Hider, who just concluded his first annual “President’s Kaizen Week.” But maximizing value while minimizing waste through human-led continuous improvement processes can sound quaint. Most manufacturers would rather talk about digital transformation, automation, and AI than poka-yoke, gemba walks and the three Ms of waste (muda, mura, muri!).

Not Tom Polen of BD, otherwise known as Becton, Dickinson and Company, No. 211 on the Fortune 500. The company sells 35 billion devices a year ranging from hypodermic needles to advanced monitoring platforms. Polen talks about lean manufacturing with the same zeal that other CEOs talk about AI. He even shares the same sensei (master teacher) with Culp, Yukio Katahira. Polen became CEO in 2020, launching BD Excellence in 2024 to scale lean practices across the company, going from 50 kaizen projects to 1,500 last year. He argues that lean is a prerequisite for leveraging AI.

“If you’re not doing lean, do lean first,” he told me. “Get those systems and capabilities and then start applying AI on top of solid processes and systems. I’m 100% convinced that AI with lean is where you get the power.”

He says lean has enabled a cultural shift, too, as the company completed the spinoff of its $3.3 billion-a-year bioscience and diagnostic solutions units earlier this month to focus on its $18.5 billion medical technology business. While BD faces pricing pressure in China and a range of challenges at home, its stock is up 19% this year while the S&P 500 is flat.

items.t: Reimagining operations with agentic AI at Toyota
sum: Toyota wants to avoid “shiny object syndrome” when it comes to emerging technology opportunities and, specifically, the shiniest object of all these days: agentic AI.

The question is, “What problem are we trying to solve, and then what’s the fit-for-purpose technology that will help our team members, our customers, and our company move forward?” says Jason Ballard, vice president of digital innovations at Toyota.1
Track the trends in technology's evolution through these short stories of tech pioneers

The company’s digital innovations group, which comprises design, technology, and functional experts, is embedded within the automotive operations and supply chain functions and plays a key role in Toyota’s digital transformation, driving impactful change across the enterprise. “We’re not operating with blinders on or just trying to optimize a single function,” Ballard explains.

Toyota has been using various forms of artificial intelligence for several years, beginning with machine learning optimization engines and, more recently, generative AI embedded into the company’s technology products. “Now we’re leaning into agentic AI,” Ballard says, “starting with single agents and working toward a system of agents to help our different operations.”

Take the company’s resource allocation process to meet customer demand. Historically, the operation had been “pretty messy,” Ballard explains, involving 75-odd spreadsheets, 50-plus team members, and hours and hours to come up with the right plans for suppliers and manufacturing teams.

The digital innovations team is building a global planning system that shrinks that team to 6 to 10 planners, allowing the remaining members to be redistributed to other, more pressing areas, and eliminating all those spreadsheets. The process starts with an AI agent that pulls in demand data, looks at supply, and walks the planning team through possible scenarios. Agentic AI “handles the routine, repetitive tasks and lets the team members make the advanced decisions around which scenarios they choose,” Ballard says. “It helps them with the constraints. It helps them optimize for revenue or other factors. It gives them models in minutes rather than all those hours of overtime.”

sum: Toyota's got a $5.7 billion mess on its hands in California. A class-action lawsuit just dropped, with three furious Mirai owners leading the charge for everyone who bought or leased these hydrogen-fuel-cell rides from 2016 onward. And let's just say, Toyota's big hydrogen dream? It's looking more like a gaslighting nightmare.

The suit throws punches at Toyota, its dealers, and even its finance wing, slamming them for allegedly pushing cars tied to what owners describe as a broken refuelling network. Hidden defects? Oh, they're all over the place—failed fills, hydrogen leaks, sketchy acceleration—while Toyota kept hyping the Mirai as some eco-friendly chariot. Reality check? Owners say half the stations were ghost towns, turning their shiny "zero-emission" rides into driveway décor.

Here's the kicker: Toyota swore the Mirai could fuel up in "about five minutes." Cue the laughter. Drivers ended up hunting for working stations like it was some post-apocalyptic road trip, only to face hours-long lines or straight-up empty pumps. Then Shell nuked its hydrogen spots last year, shrinking the network to a skeleton crew. Good luck finding fuel now.

Oh, and things get spicy—plaintiffs tossed the RICO Act into the mix, claiming Toyota ran a full-blown "deception campaign" to juice sales while ignoring the infrastructure dumpster fire. Marketing spun tales of hydrogen's golden age, but drivers got stuck holding the bag—err, the useless lease papers.

Toyota admits hydrogen access is "a challenge" and even paused Mirai sales in places like Sacramento. They're tossing out service credits and rental cars like consolation prizes, but owners aren't buying it. One thing's clear: when your car can't even move, a coupon just doesn't cut it.
